diagnostic_evidence.quote: The function $\log(2 \sin (x/2))$ is concave on $(0,2 \pi)$, and so $f(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_n)$, a sum of concave functions of linear forms, is also concave.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof correctly writes $\log|\det V|$ as a concave function $f$ of the gap variables on the polytope $\{\phi_j\ge\varepsilon,\ \sum\phi_j\le2\pi-\varepsilon\}$ and notes that the minimum is attained at an extreme point (one gap of $2\pi-n\varepsilon$, the rest $\varepsilon$), but it then ends. It never evaluates $f$ at those extreme points or compares with the equispaced value $f(\varepsilon,\ldots,\varepsilon)$. Since the equispaced point is not itself an extreme point, the claimed inequality $|\det V|\ge|\det V(1,e^{i\varepsilon},\ldots,e^{in\varepsilon})|$ does not follow from the concavity observation alone; the missing step is the finite computation showing that at a one-big-gap configuration the pairwise chord-length product equals the equispaced product (cross-cluster arcs $2\pi-d\varepsilon$ contribute $\sin(d\varepsilon/2)$). The statement is true (verified numerically in several cases), but the proof as written is incomplete.

failure_location.quote: The minimum value of $f(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_n)$ on the polytope $\sum_{j=1}^n \phi_j \le 2 \pi - \epsilon$ and $\phi_j \ge \eps$ for $j = 1,\ldots,n$ occurs at an extreme point. Every extreme point corresponds to $n+1$ angles $	heta_j$ with gaps $\eps$ for all but one pair, with a gap of $2 \pi - n \epsilon$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing evaluation: at an extreme point with gaps $\varepsilon$ except one gap of $2\pi-n\varepsilon$, count the pairwise arc distances within and across the two clusters to show $\sum_{j<k}\log(2\sin((\theta_k-\theta_j)/2))=\sum_{d=1}^n(n+1-d)\\log(2\sin(d\varepsilon/2))$, hence $f(\text{extreme})=f(\varepsilon,\ldots,\varepsilon)$ and the minimum equals the equispaced value.
issues.overall_effect: Only the proof of a20 is incomplete; its statement is true, and its sole user (a45, applied in the regime $2\pi-n\varepsilon\le2\varepsilon$ with $\delta=2\pi/(n+2)\le\varepsilon$) invokes it validly, so no downstream result is affected.
issues.title: a20: proof of the Vandermonde determinant lower bound stops before evaluating the extreme points
issues.why_classification: The statement is true and the omitted step is a routine finite computation; the only application of a20 is valid, so a short local addition to the proof repairs everything with no loss of content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In addition, by \Cref{a24}, $\Cl(\eps n/2) = \hat C \alpha(1-\alpha) \log (2/\alpha)$ for some $\hat C \in [1/\pi,2/5]$.

issues.failure_explanation: At $\alpha=1/2$ the ratio equals $\frac{\Cl(\pi/2)}{\frac14\log4}=\frac{2G}{\log2}\approx2.643$, which is not in $[\frac1\pi,\frac25]=[0.318,0.4]$; as $\alpha\to0$ or $\alpha\to1$ the ratio tends to $\pi$. The true range is $[\frac{2G}{\log2},\pi]$. Equivalently, the reciprocal ratio $\frac{\alpha(1-\alpha)\log(2/\alpha)}{\Cl(\alpha\pi)}$ does lie in $[\frac1\pi,\frac25]$, so the fraction in item 7 is inverted. The statement as written is false; it is not a case of an argument proving less than claimed (no proof is given) or of a misapplied hypothesis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the interval to the true range $[\frac{2G}{\log2},\pi]$ (equivalently, invert the ratio), which leaves a30's application and conclusion unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The only use is in a30, which requires only that $\Cl(\varepsilon n/2)=\hat C\,\alpha(1-\alpha)\log(2/\alpha)$ for some $\hat C=\Theta(1)$; since the true range $[\frac{2G}{\log2},\pi]$ is also $\Theta(1)$, a30's conclusion $\frac{M_{\mathrm n}}{M_{\mathrm w}}=\Theta(\log(2/\alpha))$ is unaffected. No formal result is invalidated.
issues.title: a24 item 7: the stated interval for the Clausen ratio is wrong (the fraction is inverted)
issues.why_classification: The statement is false as written, but the correction is immediate and the only application needs just the order of magnitude, which is unchanged; no substantive claim, rate, or guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: Applying a37 with $a=0$, $b=(m+1)\varepsilon$ (valid in case 2) gives $-\sum_{j=1}^m\log(2\sin\frac{\varepsilon j}2)=\frac{\Cl(\varepsilon(m+1))}{\varepsilon}-\frac12\log\frac{\pi}{\varepsilon}-\frac12\log\frac{\pi}{2\pi-\varepsilon m}\pm5$, whereas the stated formula is $\frac{\Cl(\varepsilon m)}{\varepsilon}+\frac12\log\varepsilon-\frac12\log(2\pi-(m+1)\varepsilon)+O(1)$. The two differ by $\log\pi+\frac12\log\frac{2\pi-(m+1)\varepsilon}{2\pi-\varepsilon m}$ plus the error of the a24(6) estimate ($\frac12\frac{\varepsilon}{2\pi-\varepsilon(m+1)}$); writing $u=2\pi-\varepsilon m$, the discrepancy is $\log\pi+\frac12\log\frac{u-\varepsilon}{u}+O(\frac{\varepsilon}{u-\varepsilon})$, which is unbounded as $u\to\varepsilon^+$ (i.e. $(m+1)\varepsilon\to2\pi^-$). Hence the $O(1)$ error in case 2 is not uniform and the stated formula is false in that boundary regime. All downstream uses avoid it: a26 and a27 are applied only when $2\pi-n\varepsilon\ge2\varepsilon$ (a46's regime, where the discrepancy is $O(1)$) or $2\pi-n\varepsilon\ge2\sqrt\varepsilon$ (a47's regime, where it is $O(\log n)$ and absorbed in a47's $O(\log(n\varepsilon(2\pi-n\varepsilon)))$ error).

failure_location.quote: If instead $\eps m>\pi$, we may apply \Cref{a37} along with the estimate \[\frac{\Cl(\eps m+\eps)-\Cl(\eps m)}\eps = -\log(2\pi-(m+1)\eps )+O(1)\] in that regime to obtain \[\spliteq{}{\-\sum_{j=1}^m\log\pare{2\sin\frac{\eps j}2} = \frac{\Cl(\eps m)}\eps+\frac12\log\eps-\frac12\log\pare{2\pi-(m+1)\eps}+O(1)}\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen a38 case 2's hypothesis to $2\pi-(m+1)\varepsilon\ge2\varepsilon$ (the regime in which all applications occur), or enlarge the error term to $O(\log\frac{2\pi-\varepsilon m}{\varepsilon})$; either preserves every downstream use and restores uniformity where the lemma is actually applied.
issues.overall_effect: a38's case-2 statement is false as a uniform claim, and a26 and a27 inherit the non-uniformity in their stated regimes (their $O(1)$ errors fail when $2\pi-\varepsilon m\approx\varepsilon$). However, every application of a26/a27 (within a46 and a47) lies in a regime where the error is $O(1)$ or $O(\log n)$ and is absorbed, so a1, a3, a4 and all main results are unaffected.
issues.title: a38: the case-2 error term is not O(1) in the boundary regime (m+1)eps ~ 2pi
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local hypothesis addition (or error-term enlargement) in a regime no result uses; the method, conclusion, rate, and advertised scope of the paper all survive, so the mathematical loss is nil.

issues.failure_explanation: By definition $2g_w(\varepsilon n+\varepsilon)=2U(\frac{\varepsilon n}2+\pi)+M_w(\varepsilon+\frac{\varepsilon n}2-\pi)^2$, so the displayed equality $e^{2g_w(\varepsilon n+\varepsilon)}=e^{-2U(\varepsilon n/2+\pi)-M_w(\varepsilon+\varepsilon n/2-\pi)^2}$ has the wrong sign on both terms. Moreover the underlying pointwise bound $e^{-2U_k(x)}\le e^{2g_w(\varepsilon n+\varepsilon)}$ on $(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon n+\varepsilon)$ fails near the node $x=k\varepsilon$ (there $e^{-2U_k(x)}\approx e^{-2U_k(k\varepsilon)}$, which can exceed $e^{2g_w(\varepsilon n+\varepsilon)}$). The intended conclusion — that the near-arc integral is exponentially negligible relative to the main term — is nevertheless true: on $(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon n+\varepsilon)$ one has $|L_k(e^{ix})|\le\prod_{j\ne k}\frac1{|\sin((k-j)\varepsilon/2)|}=e^{U_k(k\varepsilon)}$, so $e^{-2U_k(x)}=e^{-2U_k(k\varepsilon)}|L_k(e^{ix})|^2\le1$ and the integral is at most $\varepsilon(n+2)=O(n)$, exponentially smaller than $e^{2U_k(\varepsilon k)-2U(\varepsilon n/2+\pi)}\sqrt{\ldots}$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the a43 chain by the direct bound $\int_{-\varepsilon}^{\varepsilon n+\varepsilon}e^{-2U_k(x)}dx\le\varepsilon(n+2)$ (from $|L_k|\le e^{U_k(k\varepsilon)}$ on the near arc), which is $O(n)$ and hence negligible against the main term.
issues.overall_effect: Only the proof of a32 is affected; the lemma's statement is true (the correct direct estimate yields the claimed negligibility), so a33, a44, and a47, which use a32's statement, are unaffected.
issues.title: a32 proof: wrong-sign substitution for e^{2g_w(eps n+eps)} and a false intermediate bound
issues.why_classification: The proof contains a wrong-sign substitution and a false intermediate bound, but the lemma's statement is correct and the repair is a one-line direct estimate; no downstream result or rate is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Our final step is to properly select $a$. We pick $a$ to be any element of the set \[\ball(z_-,(n+1)^{1/2}r)\backslash\bigcup_{j=0}^n\ball(z,r)\\] for $r=\frac1{2R}(\eps')^2$, which is nonempty by considering the areas of each ball.

Consequently, \[\abs{a-z_-}\le(n+1)^{1/2}r<\eps'\le(\frac{\beta\ks(\mu_S,\mu)}{\rho_1})^{1/\beta}.\] Additionally, by construction $\dist(a,S)\\ge r$ and $\delta(r)=O\pare{ \log(R/\eps')\ks(\mu_S,\mu) }$, so we have the final result.

issues.failure_explanation: Two steps are unjustified as written. (1) a54's lower bound: the triangle inequality gives only $\ks(\mu_k,\mu)\ge\ks(\mu_S,\mu)-\frac1{n+1}$, which yields $\ks(\mu_k,\mu)\ge\frac12\ks(\mu_S,\mu)$ only when $\ks(\mu_S,\mu)\ge\frac2{n+1}$; the complementary case requires the separate observation $\ks(\mu_k,\mu)\ge\frac1n$ (a small ball around any $z_j$, $j\ne k$), which the paper does not mention. The claim is true, but the one-line justification is insufficient. (2) The final step: a49 is applied at $z=a$ with $\varepsilon=\dist(a,S)$, which requires $\dist(a,S)\le(\frac{\beta\ks(\mu_k,\mu)}{\rho_1})^{1/\beta}$; the proof only bounds $|a-z_-|$, while $\dist(a,S)\le|a-z_-|+\dist(z_-,S)$ with $\dist(z_-,S)$ uncontrolled ($z_-$ need not lie in $S$). Both gaps are patchable without changing the statement.

failure_location.quote: We claim that \[\eq{\label{a54}\frac12\ks(\mu_S,\mu)\le\ks(\mu_k,\mu)\le2\ks(\mu_S,\mu)}.\] To see this, note that condition (3) implies $\mu(\set z)=0$ for any $z$. In particular, we have $\ks(\mu_k,\mu_S)=\frac1{n+1}\le\min\pare{\ks(\mu,\mu_k),\ks(\mu,\mu_S)}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply the missing case split for a54's lower bound (using $\ks(\mu_k,\mu)\ge\frac1n$ when $\ks(\mu_S,\mu)\le\frac2{n+1}$) and apply a49 at $a$ with $\varepsilon=\min(\dist(a,S),(\frac{\beta\ks(\mu_k,\mu)}{\rho_1})^{1/\beta})$, which yields the same final error $O(\log\frac1s\ks(\mu_S,\mu))$.
issues.overall_effect: a10 is proved as 'a direct combination of a18 and a50', so its proof inherits these gaps; a10's statement is a soft O(.) theorem that is expected to survive the patch, and no quantitative guarantee is lost.
issues.title: a50 proof: a54 lower bound unjustified; final application of a49 at a conflates |a-z_-| with dist(a,S)
issues.why_classification: The gaps are small and the fixes are local and do not change a50's or a10's statements; no rate, regime, or guarantee is lost.
